title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 677-678 of the 'suite à la Longue Marche'). M is a rank-2 lattice with basis λ0, λ1. It carries automorphisms ρ_M and σ_M, which look like the elliptic generators of order 3/6 and 4 of SL(2,Z) ≅ Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6. M behaves as the Eisenstein lattice for ρ, since (1-ρ)(λ1-λ0) = 3λ1 (eq. 95). The underlined M denotes the associated vector-group scheme over S0 = Spec Z, and \underline{C}_K appears to be the corresponding curve or group object over a field K. Z̃_{ρ,σ} is a group scheme, embedded in (finite group of units mod 12) × M × M. It parametrises triples (μ, α0, β0) satisfying a 'cocycle' equation (94)/(96): (1-ρ)(α0 - ν''(λ1-λ0)) - (1-σ)(β0) = 0, where ν''(μ) is an integer-valued function of the component μ. So Z̃ is an extension of the finite constant group by the kernel Z̃^{0+} of the linear map M×M → M, (α,β) ↦ (1-ρ)α - (1-σ)β. On the previous page Grothendieck noted that Z̃ is smooth in characteristic ≠ 3 but not in characteristic 3.

This page diagnoses the defect. Mod 3 the linear map drops rank, so the relative dimension jumps from 2 to 3. He argues this jump is not an artefact that could be removed by ad hoc redefinition of a 'better' Z̃. The reason he gives is that over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 3 there really are 'more' automorphisms of C_K, with the same set-theoretic properties, than in other characteristics. This matches the classical fact that j = 0 = 1728 in characteristic 3, where Aut(E) has order 12.

Nevertheless he proposes a subgroup scheme of Z̃_{ρ,σ}, presumably a variant of N_{ρ,σ}, with two properties: it is smooth over Spec Z, and it coincides with Z̃ over S_{0,3} = Spec Z[1/3]. The key observation, carried out on the next page, concerns the left-hand side of (96). It always lies in the index-3 sublattice M0 = {c0λ0 + c1λ1 | c0 + c1 ≡ 0 (3)} = (1-ρ)M, the ideal (1-ω) of norm 3. One therefore regards the cocycle equation as an equation in the vector bundle \underline{M}0 rather than in \underline{M}. Over Z[1/3] the inclusion M0 → M is an isomorphism, so nothing changes there. Over F3 the map into M0 remains of full rank, so its kernel is smooth of constant relative dimension 2. The resulting subgroup is closed, flat and smooth.

In modern terms this is a standard smoothening by changing the target lattice: you factor a map of vector bundles through the saturation of its image. It resembles a dilatation or Néron-type modification. It serves Grothendieck's study of integral (over Spec Z) models of the automorphism and extension groups attached to the elliptic generators of the modular group, in the framework of the Galois–Teichmüller tower.
errors: Possible gap: only characteristic 3 is treated as exceptional. In characteristic 2 one also has j = 0 = 1728, with an even larger automorphism group (order 24). Characteristic 2 may well be harmless for this particular cocycle equation, since the relevant map involves 1-ρ, whose norm is 3. But the justification via 'more automorphisms of C_K in char 3' would apply in char 2 too, and it is not addressed here.
Not a proof: Grothendieck had earlier 'admitted' the group structure on Z̃_{ρ,σ} (p. 677), and the smoothness of the proposed subgroup is only sketched. The page breaks off mid-construction.

ideas.what: The fiber-dimension jump of the cocycle group scheme at p = 3 reflects genuinely extra automorphisms of the curve in characteristic 3, so it cannot be removed by an ad hoc redefinition.
ideas.modern_name: Extra automorphisms of the supersingular curve with j = 0 = 1728 in characteristic 3 (Aut of order 12)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Deuring); standard reference Silverman, AEC, Appendix A

ideas.what: Replace the target M of the cocycle equation by the index-3 sublattice M0 = (1-ρ)M. This yields a subgroup scheme that is smooth over Spec Z and agrees with Z̃ over Z[1/3].
ideas.modern_name: Smoothening / dilatation by saturating the image of a map of vector bundles (cf. Néron models, BLR ch. 3)

ideas.what: Identification of the sublattice {c0 + c1 ≡ 0 mod 3} with the image of 1-ρ on the Eisenstein lattice.
ideas.modern_name: The ideal (1-ω) of norm 3 in Z[ω]

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out to build smooth integral models over Spec Z of the group schemes N_{ρ,σ} / Z̃_{ρ,σ}. These encode cocycles of the elliptic generators of SL(2,Z) with values in the lattice. The construction is technically routine, but the programme of such integral models within the Teichmüller-tower context does not seem to be pursued in the literature.
missed.quote: Cependant il me semble qu'on peut construire un sous-schéma en groupes de Z̃_{ρ,σ} ... qui est lisse sur S0 = Spec(Z) ... qui coïncide avec Z̃_{ρ,σ} au-dessus de S_{0,3} = Spec Z[1/3]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of minor interest. It might matter for anyone studying integral or arithmetic versions of the Galois action on the profinite modular group and its affine extensions, but the technique itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sharply diagnoses a char-3 non-smoothness as genuine, rather than an artefact. It then applies a standard smoothening trick, restricting the target to the norm-3 ideal. Both steps are mathematically routine. The only point of interest is that this is part of an unpublished integral-model programme inside the Longue Marche continuation.
transcription_corrections: 'Z̃_{g,ν}' throughout should read Z̃_{ρ,σ}, consistent with the neighbouring pages.
'(pour le un corps alg. clos)' should read '(pour K un corps alg. clos)'.
'si le cas de car. 3' is more likely 'dans le cas de car. 3'.
'que j'avais dû noter' is possibly 'que j'aurais dû noter'.
'dans la description du haut (96)' is likely 'dans l'équation des cocycles (96)', the phrase used on the next page.
'les premiers membres arithmétiques' is likely 'les premiers membres (de l'équation) sont dans le sous-module de M correspondant à la congruence c0 + c1 ≡ 0 (3)'.
The last line should read 'et si on introduit le sous-Z-module d'indice 3 correspondant', continued as M0 on p. 678.
